name: Datalayer Agent Codemode, jupyter-server sandbox variant (local Jupyter Server it starts itself)
pinned: agent-codemode 566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea (1.1.1), code-sandboxes 1.12.4 (tag v1.12.4 = d7030b0b), jupyter_server and ipykernel from the same venv
engine: An ipykernel process on the host, started by a Jupyter Server subprocess that the sandbox launches with the host interpreter, driven over HTTP and websockets by jupyter-kernel-client. Same user, same machine, same environment as the host.
how_run: Same harness as datalayer-codemode-eval with sandbox_variant='jupyter-server'. defaults.tool_calls: CodeModeConfig.max_tool_calls defaults to None (types.py:233). It is enforced only in the host's executor.call_tool, which this variant's in-kernel MCP clients never call.

source_notes.finding: Not a host bridge. Without mcp_proxy_url, setup sends the host's MCP server configs (command, args, env) into the kernel and builds agent_codemode MCPClient objects there, so the kernel spawns its own copy of each MCP server and calls it directly (P1: 42, one call, logged by a server process the kernel started). Credentials that a server needs must therefore be readable by the kernel.

MCPClient creates its stdio session lazily with no lock, so five concurrent first calls race: four returned {'error': 'Connection closed'} as ordinary values and one succeeded (P9d). After one warm-up call the same gather ran in parallel, 202 ms host-side (P9w).

None beyond a separate process. The server is started with the caller's interpreter and inherits the host environment, so files, environment, network and os.system all work (P3, P4, P5, P12), with or without env_vars={}.

The execute timeout only bounds how long the client waits. On timeout the result is execution_ok=True with no error and the kernel keeps running the loop; the sandbox has an interrupt endpoint (_do_interrupt) but run_code does not call it on timeout.
Persistent kernel namespace across executions (P8 printed 7).
IPython tracebacks with cell line numbers and ANSI colour codes come back in the error text (P10).
One-time setup 2.6 s (Jupyter Server plus kernel start, plus binding generation run inside the kernel); median 8.8 ms per execution afterwards (P11).

surprises: The only local Datalayer variant whose tool calls work is jupyter-server, and only because the kernel runs on the host and starts its own copies of the MCP servers.
A timeout returns a blank success and leaves the kernel spinning; the next call in the same session hangs (P6b).
Concurrent cold tool calls fail silently with {'error': 'Connection closed'} dicts rather than exceptions (P9d).
The variant's default port 8888 and `python` from PATH had to be overridden through constructor arguments; CodeModeConfig has no field for either.
